To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trust in computers is influenced by the duality of warmth and competence, anthropomorphism of the computer, task advice, social blame, and the interaction between these factors.

human–computer trust is influenced by cooperative factors that are similar to those that affect interpersonal trust, and that the design of anthropomorphic computer agents can help to establish trust and to regulate trust in the long run.
trust formation and regulation in human–computer cooperation is influenced by the dualities of competence and selfish behavior, anthropomorphism and task advice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theoretical model for the investigation of cooperative human– computer interaction.
the development of a new paradigm to study trust in human–computer interaction, and the identification of new antecedents and regulation strategies for human–computer trust.

the development of a new modeling framework for the study of human–computer cooperation, and the investigation of the influence of cooperative interaction factors on the formation, and regulation, of human–computer interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trust in interdependent and goal-oriented human-computer interaction is a powerful psychological variable that influences user behavior.

trust in computers can be influenced by the way in which computers behave in cooperative interactions with users, and that the influence of cooperative interaction factors on trust formation can be explained by the universal dimension of warmth.

the presented research contributes to a better understanding of the antecedents and formation of trust in computers and provides a new method for the evaluation of trust in human–computer cooperation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed modeling paradigm can help to better understand the antecedents of human–computer cooperation and trust.

trust is a complex construct that can be influenced by a variety of cooperative interaction factors and that trust in computers is a valuable psychological variable for the evaluation of human–computer interaction.
trust in computers can be enhanced by making computers more like human partners in cooperation, by providing them with a social face.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presented modeling framework is a promising tool for the investigation of human–computer cooperation.
human–computer trust can be modeled as a dynamic psychological variable, which can be regulated through the use of anthropomorphic design features.
the modeling of human–computer cooperation is a powerful tool for the study of human–computer interaction, as well as for the development and design of human–computer interfaces.
